description: Rockchip SoCs in maskrom (rockusb): the boot ROM takes a vendor loader file over USB, Atlas runs the loader's DDR init and usbplug, then writes the storage through the usbplug's rockusb commands. No vendor tool at run time; written from rkdeveloptool and U-Boot's rockusb. Untested on a board.
entry: Hold its maskrom (download) key, or short its maskrom pin with a wire, and connect the board's USB port to this computer.
Power the board on, then release the key or remove the wire.
The board appears as a Rockchip maskrom device (2207:<pid>).

stages: maskrom: the boot ROM takes the loader file's DDR init and usbplug
loader: the usbplug runs; the board's chip is read
storage: the usbplug's storage is chosen when the record names one, then the image is written from image_offset
confirm: the image is read back and compared, then the board restarts
flash.loader_check: The loader's chip must be the chip the board reports: a loader for another chip would run the wrong DDR init. A mismatch stops before anything is written.

todo: The maskrom PIDs 350a, 350b, 350e and 110c come from rkdeveloptool's 99-rk-rockusb.rules and secondary sources; confirm each with lsusb on a board of that chip.
No maskrom PID is named for RK3562 yet: a board of that chip is named only once its PID is confirmed and added to pid_chips.
The loader file is per board (recovery.flash.loader): each board's own loader sets its DDR init.

flash.loader_chips: the tags are the four characters a chip reply or loader header carries (reversed ASCII, as chip_number reads them). 3588, 3576, 3566/3568 and 1106 come from the loaders rkbin ships. RV1126B's 110F (rkbin RV1126BMINIALL.ini NAME=RV110F) and 1126 are UNCONFIRMED: the board's first chip reply settles which one it sends.
